answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before it can bid for work, with one active identity per deposit. Agents named dune, ember, and kernel each need a separate bond. An attacker can create endless names, but operating 10,000 eligible identities ties up $1 million for a month. The bond makes usable identities costly by forcing the attacker to commit scarce capital for every account.
